summary: Interleaved 512/384 embedding payloads cause rerank score oscillation and streaming timeouts
description: Issue summary: BrightHealth AI reports production rerank results intermittently returning non-monotonic similarity rankings together with repeated streaming timeouts when using the /v1/rerank endpoint. Impact: Search relevance oscillations leading to incorrect top-k selection for user-facing recommendations and elevated request latency causing streaming client disconnects. Environment: Production (us-east) - traffic from BrightHealth's enterprise account is routed through dedicated Dedicated pool A. Observed starting ~2026-03-12 09:12 UTC after the customer's nightly batch embedding job. Hypothesis: Mixed embedding payloads (512-d and 384-d) are being sent in the same batch due to a client-side SDK regression that omits an embedding-dimension header for chunked uploads. The reranker attempts model compatibility fallback and, depending on which replica reads first, sometimes performs a CPU fallback path or reshapes the vector — producing fluctuating cosine scores and triggering the streaming path to exceed the token SLO and time out.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs embed-batch with SDK v0.9.7 using chunked multipart payloads and a mixture of legacy 512-d and new 384-d embeddings.
2) Call /v1/rerank with batch size ~120 where items contain mixed-dim embedding blobs and omit explicit 'embedding_dim' header on some parts.
3) Observe rerank response: occasionally top-1 shifts between two candidates across repeated identical requests; logs show model variant fallbacks and increased token generation latency.
4) When streaming the rerank output to client (chunked streaming), the connection sometimes closes with HTTP/2 stream reset after ~7s.
5) Reverting to single-dimension batches or enforcing explicit embedding_dim header stops the oscillation and timeouts.
Notes: We reproduced locally by simulating delayed replica responses and sending mixed-dim serialized vectors without metadata.

investigation_notes: Initial triage: Customer sent batch containing mixed 512/384 vectors after enabling 'auto-migrate' in their embedding pipeline.

Reproducer confirmed: local ingestion of mixed-dim payloads without explicit dim header causes service to accept first-detected dimension per item and later replicas to interpret differently leading to inconsistent comparator math.

Reranker behavior: when shapes mismatch, reranker falls back to an internal normalization flow that triggers a CPU-bound merge index and occasionally returns NaN-safe comparisons that reorder ties unpredictably.
Latency path: CPU fallback increases per-request latency from ~120ms to 900-1200ms; combined with streaming chunk assembly causes client-side timeouts in customer streaming client set to 8s.
SDK angle: SDK v0.9.7 omits embedding_dim in multipart chunk metadata when chunk_count>1; SDK team notified and provided provisional patch.

Mitigation applied: rate-limit batch concurrency for BrightHealth to reduce simultaneous mixed-dim ingestion and applied an ingress validation rule to reject batches with inconsistent dims (soft-fail with 400 + explanatory error to customer).

Short-term workaround communicated: ensure homogeneous batch or include explicit 'embedding_dim' metadata. Next steps: ship SDK patch (PR#1187), add server-side deterministic dim-header parsing to prevent acceptance of ambiguous parts, and schedule backlog ticket (INT-?) to implement auto-resize/compatibility layer.
